subject: Re: BrightStack discovery — elastic throughput, p95 objectives & streaming UX
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria@brightstack.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: BrightStack discovery — elastic throughput, p95 objectives & streaming UX

Thanks again for the time today. This was a helpful intro — summarizing what we covered so we can align on next steps. High-level pain and goals we discussed: 

- Pain points:
  - Inference p95 for short/interactive prompts is inconsistent: typical p95 ~1.2s but spikes to 2.5–3s under moderate load.
  - Streaming UX is choppy for our conversational widgets; first-token feels slow and causes UI flicker.
  - Cost volatility with current vendor (we see big spend for peak windows).
  - Lack of reliable autoscaling for bursts (we get 1k->10k qps in <10min during product events).

- Current stack / constraints:
  - Frontend: React on Vercel.
  - API layer: Kubernetes microservices (GKE) that forward to a mix of OpenAI hosted endpoints and our on-prem Triton fleet.
  - Authentication & data handling: some sensitive signals (PII hashed) — need to confirm retention and audit logs for compliance.

- Success criteria (what would make this a win):
  - Sustained throughput: support 1,000 qps baseline, ability to absorb 10k qps bursts with graceful degradation.
  - Latency: p95 < 350ms for short completions (<=128 tokens); first-token streaming latency under 100ms for interactive UX.
  - Predictable cost: unit economics comparable or better than current spend with transparent controls.
  - Operational controls: clear rollouts, fallbacks, and observability (per-route latency/cost).

Quick clarifying items we need from you so Redwood can scope a PoC:
1) Representative traffic shape (RPS distribution, typical request sizes, % streaming vs. single-shot).
2) A small anonymized sample of typical prompts (we can run offline benchmarks against similar models).
3) Any hard compliance constraints around retention or in-region hosting.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- Grace will share a draft MOP and an initial trial playbook (we can iterate) — aim to have it by EOD tomorrow.
- BrightStack to share traffic profile + sample prompts.
- Follow-up technical deep-dive with Sean + Aditya to review model choices, batching & KV-cache strategies, and autoscaling policies.

Attachments: I dropped a quick sketch of our suggested trial flow and a blank MOP template (will send final by EOD).

Thanks — excited to dig in.

—Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of ML Infrastructure, BrightStack


From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@brightstack.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 16:10:43 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightStack discovery — elastic throughput, p95 objectives & streaming UX

Maria — great notes, thanks. Confirming everything below and adding a few pragmatic hypotheses we want to validate in the PoC. I attached the draft MOP, an example system diagram, and a short trial checklist (filenames in attachments).

Recap + Redwood hypotheses to validate in the run: 
1) Batching + KV caching will reduce p95 for short completions significantly vs your current OpenAI staging traffic (expect 3–5x improvement for <=128-token workloads).
2) Streaming first-token improvements are primarily network+kernel-selection related; with a streaming-optimized runtime and smaller model slices we should achieve <100ms median first-token in the POC.
3) Autoscaling policy: continuous batching + short-lived hot replicas plus burst autoscale (pre-warm based on traffic signals) should smooth 10x bursts without p95 regressions.

Proposed immediate next steps (items we will own):
- I will attach the PoC MOP (MOP-draft.pdf) — includes target traffic, test harness, success criteria, and rollback plan.
- Sean will propose 2 windows for a 2-hour technical deep-dive this week (target: Tue/Wed 10–12 PST).
- Aditya will outline one quick benchmark script and a list of infra metrics we need (GPU utilization, queue latencies, kernel mismatch rate).

Can you confirm the traffic profile (RPS by minute) and attach 10–20 representative prompts (can be redacted)? Also confirm whether retention/anonymization is sufficient for Redwood to run baseline load tests in our hosted sandbox.

I'll follow up with calendar invites and the MOP attachment.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: MOP-draft.pdf, bs-system-arch.png, redwood-trial-steps.docx

Thanks both — quick clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:

- When we said "10k qps bursts" that was aggregate across a federation of endpoints; for the initial PoC we only need to validate a single region slice of ~2k qps (apologies for the fuzzy language).
- Data retention: we can provide anonymized logs for trial benchmarking; any persistent storage with customer content will need to remain in us-west region and satisfy a 30-day deletion policy.
- Security: we'll want to see how Redwood surfaces audit logs and KMS integration during the PoC.

I'll upload the redacted prompt set and a minute-by-minute RPS export to the Drive link Maria shared by EOD.

—Elliot
